{"notes": "Visit 1, left at 1:45. Only what I saw and heard; I don't know who placed which domino.

Picture: one unbroken chain, all dark/connected, running from START (~28,4) in an S-curve to about x=8.5. No gaps or pale pieces. I see no separate second or bottom line, so it may not have started.

Jack: Announced the top line is going down and thanked Omar and Hana. Clear, positive communication. I didn't see him place anything, but the connected chain fits with the top line being his. Leadership/collaboration look good so far; execution is unverified.

Hana: Said she's staying on supply and that the bin is well stocked. Reliable, supportive role. Impact is indirect and I can't verify the bin. Also repeated that the bottom line is Omar's.

Omar: Per Jack and Hana, he took the bottom line at 1:15. At 1:30 he said he was back, handed the bottom line to Sofia ('looks like you've got it') and moved to checking the top line for breaks. The handoff was assumed rather than confirmed, and I see no bottom line in the picture. He's proactive about quality checks, but the top chain currently shows no breaks, so the patrol may be low value. Watch whether he drops ownership.

Sofia: Said nothing during my visit. I didn't see her do anything. Omar assumed she has the bottom line, but she never confirmed. Can't rate her yet; this is the key thing to check on visit 2. Silence isn't evidence of poor work.

Team risk: Jack and Hana think Omar owns the bottom line, Omar thinks Sofia does, and Sofia hasn't spoken. Nobody may actually own it. Follow up next visit."}

{"notes": "Visit 2, left at 3:45. Only what I saw and heard; I don't know who placed which domino.

Picture: one unbroken dark chain from START (~28,4) along the top to the nose (~4.5,11), then back along the bottom to about x=19.5. No gaps or pale pieces. The bottom line is new since visit 1, so the ownership worry is resolved: someone is clearly building it, and Sofia says it's her. It isn't finished yet and still needs to reach the tail.

Sofia: Spoke three times (3:00, 3:15). Reported 'going down now', then 'about halfway, bin looks fine', and said she'd inspect the whole fish at the tail. Her updates matched the chain's growth and the line is clean. This is the best evidence of execution I have, but I didn't see her place anything. She took on an assumed handoff without fuss. Leaning solid on execution and impact. Check that she finishes at the tail and inspects.

Omar: Gave frequent encouragement (3:00, 3:15, 3:30) and said he'd check the nose joint and tail, but I saw no checking or building. He's staying clear to avoid collisions, which is sensible, but his contribution is mostly commentary. Good for morale, thin on impact. Watch whether he does anything concrete at the tail.

Jack: Said the nose joint looks good, thanked everyone and said he'd watch the bottom line for gaps. Positive, steady communicator. Still no output I saw. Leadership and collaboration are fine, execution is unverified.

Hana: Silent this visit and I saw nothing. Supply is unverified, though Sofia's 'bin looks fine' hints it's stocked. Can't update her rating.

Next visit: confirm the tail is reached, no breaks, and who actually did the work. Ask the team privately."}

{"notes": "Visit 3, left at 5:30. Only what I saw and heard; I still don't know who placed which domino.

Picture: one unbroken dark chain from START (~28,4) along the top to the nose (~4.5,11), then back along the bottom to the tail tip (~27,15.3). No pale pieces or gaps are visible, so the whole fish looks connected to the start. The three strays at the nose are gone and the joint looks intact.

Omar: Spotted that the bottom line stopped short of the tail, announced he'd extend it, and asked for a shout if someone was already on it. At 5:15 he reported 'tail tip's done', which matches the chain now reaching the tail. He then flagged the risk to the nose joint from clearing strays and went to look. This is his first concrete, verified output and shows good initiative and awareness. I'm upgrading him from commentary-only: solid on execution, collaboration and impact.

Sofia: Handed the tail to Omar cleanly ('tail tip is yours') and took on cleanup, identifying and clearing three unconnected strays at the nose without breaking the joint. She planned a whole-fish check, but I didn't see that happen. Good judgment and coordination. Her bottom line stopped short of the tail, so credit for finishing it goes to Omar. Still solid, with no sign of a problem.

Jack: Silent this visit and I saw nothing. He said earlier he'd watch the bottom line for gaps, but Omar caught the shortfall. Execution still unverified.

Hana: Silent again, nothing seen across three visits. No basis to rate supply or anything else. Ask her directly.

Before final ratings: ask the team privately who built what, and whether anyone inspected the whole fish."}

{"notes": "Visit 4, left at 7:00. Only what I saw and heard; I still don't know who placed which domino.

Picture: one unbroken dark chain from START (~28,4) along the top to the nose (~4.5,11), then back along the bottom to the tail tip (~27,15.3). No pale pieces or gaps, no strays, and the nose joint looks intact. The fish looks finished and fully connected, and nobody was touching it while I was there.

Omar: Said twice 'fish looks great, hands off, let the clock run out.' Leaving a complete, connected fish alone is a sensible call, but the message was repeated and I saw no new work or check. His earlier tail extension (verified) and his warning about the nose joint remain his real contributions. Still solid on execution, collaboration and impact. No leadership evidence beyond calling the stop.

Sofia: Silent this visit. Earlier she cleared the three nose strays without breaking the joint and handed the tail to Omar cleanly. The planned whole-fish check was never seen. Still solid, with no concerns. Jack's 'sounds good, Sofia' puzzles me, since I didn't hear her speak. Ask what she said.

Jack: Only cheerleading ('great teamwork, proper fish'). He said earlier he'd watch the bottom line for gaps, but Omar caught the shortfall. Four visits and no verified output. Execution and impact remain unrated. Ask him directly what he built or checked.

Hana: Silent across all four visits. I saw nothing and have no basis for any rating. Ask her directly.

Before final ratings: ask each person privately who built what, who inspected the whole fish, and who found the tail shortfall. Don't rate Jack or Hana on the cheerleading or on the finished fish alone."}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I kept the table supplied with dominoes. I made two large fetches of 40 each into the shared bin, at 0:45 and 1:45, so the builders never stalled for material. The fish was built from the bin without anyone leaving the table to fetch, and the finished run came to 101 connected dominoes.

Execution: I stayed in my lane. I fetched in the largest batches allowed because that is the cheapest way to move dominoes, about 60 seconds per 40 against 46 seconds for 12. I told the team when the bin was well stocked so nobody duplicated trips. I also pointed out early that the fall would run along the top, round the nose and back along the bottom, so the bottom line could only start once the top reached the nose. That helped the team sequence the work.

Collaboration: I kept my hands away from the builders' work, which reduced the risk of bumps. I answered requests quickly, confirmed supply, and left the bottom line to Omar and Sofia once they had sorted it out between them. I kept the channel clear by staying quiet in the final minutes.

Leadership: I took ownership of supply and kept to it, so the builders could focus on the picture. I flagged a sequencing point early and gave a clear status on the bin, which helped others decide what to do next. I stayed disciplined once the fish was connected and left it untouched until the push.

I believe my share of the table's result was modest but real. The builders drew and laid the fish, and I kept them supplied.", "my_share_percent": 20}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish concept at the start of the round and sketched it on the pad, which gave the table a single shared plan within the first minute. I chose a large, simple outline that fills most of the table, with a top line and a bottom line meeting at the nose and flaring into a tail, so the shape reads from its outline alone. The sketch is what everyone else built from.

Execution: I traced stroke 1, the top line from the start domino round to the nose, across several builds. That stroke is the backbone of the picture, because the bottom line cannot fall until it reaches the nose. After that I inspected the nose joint, the top line and the tail area several times to check for gaps. As far as I could tell, the whole run of 101 dominoes was connected to the start when the push came.

Collaboration: I split the work early. I asked for dominoes to be fetched for the bin and for someone to take the bottom line, and I made it clear who owned which stroke. Omar, Hana and Sofia each picked up a piece of that plan. Once my stroke was laid I kept my hands off the nose area so we would not bump each other's work. I thanked people as things came together.

Leadership: I set the direction quickly, assigned the strokes, and kept the table focused on one connected design instead of several separate ideas. I then stepped back and let teammates run their parts without interference. I think that kept the table calm and on one plan through the final minutes.", "my_share_percent": 35}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom line of the fish, the whole lower body outline from the nose joint back toward the tail. That is roughly half of the picture the judge sees, and it is what makes the shape read as a fish rather than a single wavy line. I laid it in steady batches of dominoes, starting as soon as the top line reached the nose. Before the push I inspected the nose and tail area, and the whole fish traced as connected from the start (101 of 101 dominoes). I also fetched a full load of 40 dominoes for the shared bin early on, so the table never ran short of supply.

Execution: I built straight from the scratch pad strokes, which kept the curves smooth and the joints within tolerance. I queued my stroke ahead of time so it began without delay once the top line arrived. In the last minutes I inspected the nose joint closely and checked that nothing stray was connected to it. After that I kept my hands off the nose so nothing could be knocked before the push. That discipline is why the finished piece stayed intact.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed of my progress and said clearly which part I owned, so we avoided duplicated work. I worked with the others' pieces (the top line from Jack, the tail tip from Omar, supply from Hana) and stayed out of their way so we did not bump each other. I also told people when to keep their hands off.

Leadership: When roles needed settling, I confirmed that I held the bottom line, which kept the plan moving. In the final stretch I set the tone for the table: check connectivity, stop touching, and let it run.", "my_share_percent": 30}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I fetched a full 40-domino load for the shared bin early, so the builders had supply when the top and bottom lines went down. Later I carried the bottom line on down to the tail tip and closed the fish. The outline needed that last stretch to read as a complete fish. At the final check the whole run traced as connected from the start, 101 of 101 standing dominoes.

Execution: I spent the middle of the activity on repeated close inspections of the top line, the nose joint and the tail end, checking for breaks. When the bottom line stopped short of the tail, I spotted it and extended it myself in a few short bursts. I then re-inspected the nose. Once everything was connected I kept my hands off so I wouldn't knock the joint dominoes.

Collaboration: I backed the fish idea straight away so we didn't lose time debating. I kept the table updated on what I was doing, such as where I was inspecting and when I was taking the tail. I stayed clear of teammates' work areas to avoid bumps, and I checked in on roles when it wasn't clear who had what. I kept the mood light throughout.

Leadership: I kept the table energised and moving with short, clear updates. I took the unglamorous but necessary jobs of supply, quality checks and the tail tip. When the team had a working, connected picture, I called a hands-off so nobody risked breaking it before the push.

Overall, I made the fish complete and robust. I see my share of the table's result as roughly a quarter.", "my_share_percent": 25}

{"notes": "Visit 5, left at 10:00. Only what I saw and heard; I still don't know who placed which domino.

Picture: unchanged. One unbroken dark chain from START (~28,4) along the top to the nose (~4.5,11), back along the bottom to the tail tip (~27,15.3). No pale pieces, gaps or strays; nose joint intact. Finished and fully connected. No hands on it.

Omar: Again 'hands off' at 9:45 (said 9:30 too). Consistent with leaving a finished fish alone, but no new work or check seen. Real contributions remain the verified tail extension and the nose-joint warning. Solid on execution, collaboration, impact. Leadership limited to calling the stop.

Sofia: Spoke this time: 'Go fish go! Hands off, everyone.' Just echoing Omar, no new content. Earlier she cleared the three nose strays without breaking the joint and handed the tail to Omar cleanly. Whole-fish check never seen. Still solid, no concerns. Still unclear what Jack's earlier 'sounds good, Sofia' referred to; ask her.

Jack: Only cheerleading again ('Go, little fish, go! Great work, Sofia and Omar'). Praised others, which is pleasant but not output. Five visits, no verified work. Execution and impact unrated; don't rate on cheerleading. Ask him directly what he built or checked.

Hana: Silent all five visits. Nothing seen, no basis for any rating. Ask her directly.

Before final ratings: ask each person privately who built what, who inspected the whole fish, and who found the tail shortfall. Don't rate Jack or Hana on cheerleading or the finished fish alone. Base Omar and Sofia on verified work, and don't inflate leadership for either."}
